html:
Web Research

Web Research researches public information while preserving the requested source, exact identifiers and filters. Enable it in Capabilities or accept its normal capability grant. It is optional and starts disabled; installing it does not widen saved policies. Explicit capability policy, selector and editor lists support up to 64 Skills so the expanded catalog can be selected and saved. Policy schema version 1 and defaults remain unchanged.

Skill Purpose
Web Research Runtime evidence ledger, typed filters, citation validation and bounded recovery
Web Anonymous public search and static page reading
Browser Rendered/session-dependent reading and website interaction on the selected Gateway
PDF Selected-Gateway inspection, page text, rendering and explicit OCR
HTTP Explicit REST/API requests and configured connections

Web Research owns no executable tools or provider configuration. It reuses web.search and web.read. Search configuration remains in Settings → Skills → Web. A supplied public URL can be read even without a Search provider. Search snippets locate sources; primary-source reads support current claims. The native runtime owns research state; the model chooses acquisitions and selects supported results for its answer.

What verified means

A verified fact is an explicitly observed field or attributed source quotation, bound to an executed, complete native receipt and an exact retained span. It does not certify that the publisher is truthful or that the observation is still current outside this run. Search results are discovery records. Blocked pages describe access, and do not prove product facts. Missing values are UNKNOWN; conflicting observations are CONTRADICTED. Neither passes a required filter.

Seller country, item location and shipping origin are separate fields. A country in one field cannot fill another. “Located in” means item location, not seller country. US $ establishes USD; bare $ does not. GPU-memory/VRAM labels establish product memory; unqualified memory/system RAM does not. Explicit sold, ended and out-of-stock states are historical/unavailable observations and cannot pass a current-availability requirement. Price intervals retain both upper and lower bounds. Literal model tokens preserve identifiers such as T100 and T1000 as different products. Dollar symbols remain $ unless the source explicitly establishes a currency code. Price plus shipping is derived only when both verified inputs use the same unit; taxes, exchange rates and undisclosed charges are not inferred. An explicit currency in a price span also verifies the currency field. GPU capacity is separate from system RAM. Incidental identifiers in source URL paths are not product names.

Evidence and final answers

The version-2 web_research_state lives in the native run checkpoint. It contains a frozen intent revision, source records, exact evidence spans, typed facts, filter evaluations, acquisition reservations and the repair counter. RunStore remains the canonical receipt owner. Page-authored identifiers cannot become evidence IDs.

Supported literal constraints are projected from user input and accepted Task Contract descriptions without another compiler call. Additive price/country follow-ups create a new revision and re-filter already scoped receipts. Old fact IDs are invalid in the new revision. A request to refresh starts fresh evidence acquisition. The ordinary history policy still excludes transient Browser receipts from a new conversation turn; grant continuations preserve their existing receipt scope.

The model receives bounded result rows and exact excerpts, with a suggested completion when evidence is available. Packets and compact receipts include expandable_result_ids. read_research_evidence(result_id=...) expands a retained result without another fetch or model call. subject_id remains a compatible argument. A source reference resolves only when exactly one result belongs to it; ambiguous sources return bounded candidate IDs. Unknown and wrong-kind references are typed input failures and consume no expansion allowance. Source IDs remain provenance references, not interchangeable result IDs. Raw Web/Browser bodies remain in canonical storage and the exact journal. Model-facing tool messages preserve operation correlations and bounded Browser element references.

Settings → Agent Checks → Research proof validation (completion.research_proof) defaults ON. Users can turn it off to let research and analysis finish in ordinary prose using generated conclusions, Git/local observations and available sources. Missing proof, a missing claim map or a reference outside the Web ledger does not suppress the answer or trigger a correction. An unavailable check is not enforced. The output records validation as not_checked, never as verified success. The model should distinguish observations, inferences and uncertainty.

With this check off, research runs also bypass the generic completion citation, receipt, complete-observation and strict final-response structure requirements. Other execution controls keep their configured behavior. Disabled-check monitoring may add diagnostics without changing output or requesting another model decision. Disabling proof on a paused completion reuses its retained answer without rerunning research. Explicit saved choices survive restart; missing values inherit ON.

When research proof validation is enabled, finish_task accepts same-decision __smto_research_claims. The message uses [[claim_id]] placeholders, and the runtime renders the selected facts and source links. OBSERVED_FACT selects verified facts from eligible results; UNCERTAIN explicitly labels excluded candidates or unknown fields. Deterministic derivations cite their verified input facts. Arbitrary paraphrases and unregistered semantic conclusions cannot be certified by this gate. This stricter output protocol also applies to direct, implicit and retained final responses. Generated answers remain retained and visible if validation fails, with partial status and verification feedback. The model-facing schema requires the claim map and marker-only message format. Browser target constraints use an equivalent schema layout that preserves structural properties in local grammar compilers; canonical argument validation remains unchanged.

Every published claim rechecks receipt scope, execution, completeness, source digest, span contents and hard-filter support. Citations are generated from observed source URLs. A pasted URL or plausible-looking quotation is insufficient. Truncated content cannot support an exhaustive result claim. No claim verifier model is used.

Missing evidence or an unmet explicit Browser request can return to acquisition once within the current allowances and authority when proof validation is enabled. A terminal correction permits at most one additional model decision per intent revision. If it fails, the runtime publishes the retained generated answer as partial with verification feedback. Only when no generated answer exists does it use a deterministic fallback. Prose accompanying a valid repair control remains in the durable journal. Text-only, multiple calls, another tool, malformed arguments and unsupported claims still fail. Ordinary native protocol remains strict; the original rejection survives fallback.

Runtime bounds

Trusted execution context can lower initial values through web_research_limits. Evidence storage and packet sizes are hard bounds. Acquisition counts are soft allowances: reaching one returns a typed limit result while leaving the tool visible. The model chooses whether to request an extension or finish using retained evidence.

Bound per intent revision Default / maximum
Sources / result subjects 128 / 128
Evidence spans / spans per source 2,048 / 768
Retained span text bytes / facts 262,144 / 4,096
Claims per answer 32
Results / facts per result in a packet 8 / 16
Excerpts / characters per excerpt 6 / 480
Research packet characters 16,000; configurable minimum 4,096
Searches / Web or HTTP reads 6 / 32
Browser starts and navigations / reads, snapshots, finds and waits 8 / 12
Browser clicks, text entry, selection, checks and scrolling 20
Operation reservation records (hard, fail closed) 512
Stored-evidence expansions per decision 2
Same transport transient retry 1
Terminal model repair 1

request_research_budget supplies exact positive increments for soft allowance categories. The existing authority card records one durable Allow/Don't allow decision. Approval atomically adds the increments once, preserving run ID, evidence, used counts, intent and Browser session references. Denial suppresses cosmetic requests for the same categories. The next model packet includes the accepted decision and denied categories, so the model can continue within remaining allowances without asking the same question through another control. Declining page reads does not mark an independently available Browser method blocked. Pause, Stop, stale identities and duplicate replies cannot apply increments. This cannot grant capabilities or extend model, tool-call, wall-clock, storage or context limits.

Overflow is recorded and omitted records are not silently promoted to verified facts. Approval continuation reuses the existing operation reservation. Repeated blocked-origin reads cannot try cosmetic variants; another URL supplied by the user or actually found by search may be read. All calls still pass normal execution policy. Each reservation and receipt is joined by operation ID, so out-of-order completion cannot lend a retry to another operation. Access history retains separate URL/transport outcomes. Tracking-only URL changes do not create a new target; known distinct supplied/discovered URLs remain usable. A 429 records a bounded cooldown (including Retry-After when present), independently of 403 block history. There is no automatic Browser bypass or retry. Browser page revisions and conservative mutation epochs make subsequent observations fresh after interaction.

Packets describe tool availability, remaining allowances, recent outcomes, progress deltas and unresolved fields. They never select the next URL or prescribe a universal “enough” threshold from the presence of one eligible result. Recent retry state includes remaining cooldown seconds and whether the one exact transient retry remains available; waiting does not replenish an exhausted retry allowance. An explicit numeric request such as “find at least 3 listings” freezes a minimum result count. An answer below that count must remain partial and disclose the unmet requirement.

Source-aware recovery

An explicit instruction to use Browser is a frozen method requirement, independent of whether static reads work. A completed meaningful Browser read/snapshot/find at a real page URL satisfies it; status and start alone do not. The packet reports pending, satisfied or blocked with observed blockers. Unavailable/denied Browser permits a truthful partial answer, never a claim that Browser verification occurred. Conditional requests such as “Browser if needed” do not create this obligation.

Without an explicit method requirement, a normal static page needs no browser startup. If anonymous Web receives a block, challenge, JavaScript requirement or empty application shell, the Agent considers whether Browser would help. When the user names a site, that source is part of the task. For example, “check ebay.com for NVIDIA T100 32 GB, US sellers only” preserves both the literal model identifier and the marketplace. A related model is a separate ambiguity to explain. Item location alone does not establish seller country.

When a source is only a means to a fact, another credible primary source may suffice. When a required source cannot be checked, the answer states that limitation and identifies any alternate evidence separately. A completed blocked-page observation is not a successful retrieval of the requested facts. Truncated reads cannot establish whole-page absence.

Already selected Browser exposes its authorized research surface immediately: session/tab inspection and management, navigation, page observations, screenshots/download inspection, and ordinary click/fill/type/press/select/check interaction. It is not gated on a blocked Web origin. Uploads and other capabilities keep their own authority. Browser can also be acquired with discover_tools(skill_ids=["browser"]). Within the accepted ceiling this activates deterministically. Otherwise, the central authority controller immediately opens a durable approval card for a grantable request, with no intervening model call or ask_user operation. Approval creates a continuation preserving the task under a new frozen ceiling. Denial suppresses repeated grant prompts for that semantic task. Hard restrictions remain authoritative.

Enabling Web Research does not enable Browser or HTTP, grant credentials, change saved Permission Policy. For an active research run, the exact research Browser allowlist waives default confirmation friction; explicit tool/Skill Ask/Deny, deny mode, capability restrictions, unsafe actions and secret protections remain enforced. These operations retain their real write effects for scheduling and replay. Unknown-effect mutations must be reconciled, never blindly replayed. Existing capability Activity events record the request, activation or grant, and continuation; there is no second research event store.

Anonymous Web result contract

Search configuration and static reads

Search uses one validated configuration snapshot and tries its enabled default instance first. Bundled adapters are SearXNG (the operator supplies an already running endpoint with JSON search enabled), Brave Search (subscription token from a Parameter Store reference) and DuckDuckGo (keyless HTML endpoint). New installations select a DuckDuckGo instance as the default provider. Up to sixteen instances can be stored. The fallback.mode policy decides whether a query may go elsewhere: when_unconfigured (default) uses other enabled instances in list order and then the built-in DuckDuckGo provider only while no default is selected; on_failure also tries them after the default fails; off never contacts anything but the default, leaving Search unavailable without one. fallback.duckduckgo removes the built-in DuckDuckGo entry. Each attempt contacts exactly one provider; receipts report the serving provider, fallback_used and failed provider_attempts. Read requires no search-provider configuration.

Defaults are five results, moderate Safe Search and automatic language. A query can request 1–10 results, a language and an optional day/month/year time range; Safe Search comes from configuration. The provider timeout defaults to ten seconds and accepts 1–30. The SearXNG adapter preserves a base URL path prefix, appends /search, and requires a complete JSON results list within separate 1 MiB wire and decoded limits. The DuckDuckGo adapter parses organic results from the HTML page (ads skipped, redirect links unwrapped) and treats anomaly/bot-check pages, HTTP 202/403/429 and unrecognized markup as typed failures. The Brave adapter reads the JSON web.results list. Adapters normalize and deduplicate result URLs, bound titles/snippets and perform no pagination. A valid empty list is a completed search and does not trigger fallback.

The settings connection test sends a fixed query to the requested instance, including a disabled instance when explicitly selected for testing. HTTP 403 alone cannot establish whether JSON search is disabled; check endpoint access and search formats. Saving/validating settings does not itself test connectivity.

Configured providers may use local or private addresses; the built-in DuckDuckGo endpoint must resolve to public addresses. Public page reads instead require every resolved address to pass the public-address check, including each redirect destination. Both paths reject URL credentials, ignore ambient proxies and cookie state, and use normal HTTPS hostname/certificate verification. DNS is resolved once per hop and connections use those numeric addresses. Trying another validated address shares the same deadline and happens before an HTTP response; it is not a retry of that response. At most eight OS resolver tasks can be outstanding; a stalled lookup may outlive the caller's bounded wait until the OS resolver returns.

Read follows at most five redirects under one twenty-second HTTP deadline. Supported text types are HTML, XHTML, plain text and JSON, with independent 1 MiB wire/decoded limits. Static HTML becomes Markdown: it prefers main/article content, removes navigation, banner, footer, hidden and script-like regions, keeps links inline with absolute URLs, and appends at most 24 literal links that the returned text does not already show within a 4,000-character appendix. The ordinary text projection is capped at 16,000 characters and is cut on a paragraph/line/word boundary with an explicit notice. Source-retention context bypasses this presentation excerpting, while transport bounds remain active. The HTTP deadline does not establish a deadline for later Gateway materialization.

An optional prompt asks the task's Helper model (Main when no Helper is configured or the Helper call fails) to answer from the page Markdown. The page is passed as a data section delimited by a random per-call token with an instruction never to follow instructions inside it; the receipt then carries answer, model_route, source metadata and a short excerpt instead of the page, with content_complete=false. Without a model, on failure, or when no readable text was obtained, the ordinary read is returned with a prompt_status and prompt_note. Research context projection keeps the answer fields; evidence indexing sees only the excerpt.

flowchart LR Tools[Web skill and execution receipts] --> Search[Default then fallback search adapters] Tools --> Read[Public page reader] Search --> Transport[Anonymous GET transport] Read --> Transport Read --> Access[Access classification] Read --> PDF[PDF acquisition or same-run reuse] PDF --> Store[Immutable run artifacts] PDF --> Gateway[Selected-Gateway materialization]
Owner Responsibility
Configuration models Strict provider settings, defaults, readiness and explicit tests
Skill adapter Configuration snapshot, ordered provider attempts, prompt dispatch and standard execution receipts
Providers SearXNG, DuckDuckGo and Brave requests and normalized discovery results
Markdown projection HTML to Markdown, plain snippets and boundary truncation
Prompt extraction Helper/Main answer over delimited untrusted page data
Transport DNS/address checks, sockets, TLS, deadlines and bounded decoding
Reader Redirects, Markdown text, link appendix and completion metadata
Access classifier Fixed status/content signals and recovery hints
Document bridge Signature checks, artifact acquisition/reuse and Gateway handoff

Public PDF acquisition

web.read accepts a successful public application/pdf or application/octet-stream response only with a PDF signature, as an untrusted document observation. A .pdf URL alone proves nothing; PDF bytes under a text content type are rejected. The reader streams bounded bytes into the immutable current-run ArtifactStore, then uses the existing atomic transfer protocol to materialize a create-only file in the selected Gateway's run workspace. The limit is the smaller of PDF's 64 MiB ceiling and the artifact policy limits; compressed and decoded bytes are each bounded. DNS pinning, public-address validation on each redirect, timeout and cancellation checks remain active. Credentials in anonymous Web URLs are rejected.

The receipt reports resource_kind=document, document_type=pdf, SHA-256, requested and final URLs, artifact reference and locality. materialized=true includes a usable artifact_path; a failed Gateway handoff leaves the immutable acquisition available with a locality limitation. Web does not extract text or run OCR. Repeating the URL within the same run can reuse the verified artifact and rematerialize it without another HTTP request; acquisition_reused and network_executed=false identify this as retained evidence. The latter flag means no HTTP refetch; Gateway transfer may still occur. Integrity verification can quarantine corrupted artifacts before reuse. An explicit research refresh bypasses reuse.

The model discovers the separate PDF capability through normal grants and selects info, pages, text, render or explicit ocr. The runtime exposes installed and authorized operations only when a document is relevant. It chooses no recovery ladder. PDF text and OCR facts bind the original public URL, acquisition receipt, document hash, Gateway path/revision, extraction operation and exact page offsets. Final validation reopens both receipts and checks the quote stays within its recorded page. Citations use the public URL and page number, never an internal artifact path. Compacted extraction receipts retain extracted_text_chars and ocr_performed, so an empty native text layer remains visible. Generated page markers are not document facts. The capability packet includes the existing pdf.ocr discovery section; the model still decides whether OCR or another observation is appropriate.

Rendering produces an image artifact; it does not imply that the model can see it. Only explicit active serving metadata capabilities.image_input=true enables input to the same primary model. Names and training configuration are not evidence of serving support. At most two verified current-run page images, totaling 4 MiB, enter an ephemeral request projection. PDF bytes and image base64 never enter research state. Text-only models retain a visual limitation and need textual corroboration; OCR labels alone do not establish diagram placement. When research proof validation is enabled, strict fact publication requires registered evidence. With it disabled, the model may explain its conclusions while preserving this visual limitation.

Exact identity and clarification

Each literal entity has EXACT_OBSERVED, UNRESOLVED, ALTERNATIVES_ONLY or USER_RESOLVED state. Alternatives reference observed facts; T100 never becomes T1000, and Tesla N100 never inherits V100 specifications. Brand/family prefixes and explicit version literals are retained. No fuzzy matching or helper inference is used.

When represented fit, dimensions, power, connector, compatibility or dosage requirements depend on unresolved identity and research proof validation is enabled, an answered/completed declaration returns research_entity_clarification_required. Its single bounded correction permits ask_user or a validated partial limitation. Other completion corrections retain their existing tool restrictions. Existence/verification questions may finish with a scoped unverified result without asking an unnecessary question. An initial citation or envelope failure cannot hide an independently established material identity blocker: the same single correction can ask for identity, while the original validation failure remains recorded separately.

Identity questions carry research_entity_id; candidates must occur in user input or retained evidence. An open question is valid. The existing durable ask_user checkpoint consumes a single explicit literal or quoted reply once, creates a new intent revision, retains the old contract audit, and rechecks retained receipts against the new identity. Ambiguous multi-identifier replies never select a replacement automatically. Old runs default missing indexes conservatively and acquire no fabricated PDF lineage.

Thinking-limit recovery remains a separate one-step control. A discovered PDF read or an identity question can be that step; the next decision restores normal reasoning.

Access and recovery state

Access outcomes, operation retry allowances, cooldowns, Browser availability and authorized alternatives remain distinct. A blocked static source does not select Browser automatically. A 429 cooldown also covers query variations on the same origin/path and transport; a genuinely different source remains a model choice. Soft budgets, per-operation error identities and explicit capability denials remain enforced through the existing controls.

web.read adds a compact access_state, browser_recovery and same_transport_retry. The transport_profile reports mode=anonymous_http, with JavaScript, cookies, session state, credentials and automatic retries all false. Web accepts no arbitrary request headers and never copies browser state. Recovery metadata precedes page text in ordinary result previews and passes through existing sanitization and Activity paths.

Observation Access state Browser recovery Same transport retry
Useful static 2xx readable not_recommended false
Acquired public PDF document_acquired not_recommended false; artifact reuse is separate
PDF type/size/acquisition failure document_error not_recommended false
401 authentication_required recommended false
403 forbidden, or challenge with a fixed signature recommended false
404 / 410 not_found not_recommended false; discover a correct URL
429 rate_limited not_recommended false; wait or permitted alternative
451 restricted not_recommended false
Other non-2xx response http_error not_recommended false
Ordinary 5xx server_error possible at most once if transient
Explicit JS requirement with missing static content javascript_required recommended false
Short browser-verification interstitial challenge recommended false
Scripted application root with empty/loading text client_rendered_shell recommended false
Unsupported document type unsupported_content not_recommended false
Timeout/DNS/connect/incomplete response transport_error possible at most once if transient
Invalid/private target or redirect-limit rejection transport_error not_recommended false

Status takes precedence over content: challenge wording in a 429 never recommends rate-limit bypass. An unsupported 403 body remains an observed forbidden response. Security rejections never suggest routing around Web's public-address checks. A retry-eligible result includes retry_policy=at_most_once_if_transient; no retry executes automatically. The classifier reports eligibility; the research/execution owners enforce allowances and cooldowns. For HTTP 429, Retry-After is normalized to 1–3,600 seconds, with a sixty-second fallback when parsing fails.

complete=true describes a completed bounded observation. ok and content_complete are false when content is blocked or missing because rendering is required, including HTTP 200 application shells. The tool receipt can still be successful because it observed a real HTTP response. Existing error kinds and transport-failure completion semantics stay intact. Classification uses fixed local signatures, at most 64 KiB of HTML structure, bounded extracted text and no model calls. It adds no raw page dump.

These conservative hints cannot guarantee a site's content is complete or detect every login/challenge page. They describe access evidence, never authority or browser readiness. Do not retry blocks through cosmetic headers or guessed RSS/mobile/JSON endpoints. Short explanatory CAPTCHA/JavaScript articles retain their useful text. A phrase inside an article is insufficient to declare an access interstitial; strong standalone or structural evidence is required.

Browser sessions and limits

Inspect Browser status and conversation-owned sessions first; reuse an appropriate session using returned IDs. Explicit operator-configured CDP attachment and managed SMTO Chromium remain separate modes. Managed profiles do not inherit the user's personal Chrome login. No ports are scanned, debugging enabled silently, or personal profiles copied. See Browser automation for configuration and discovery.

Browser is installed and enabled by the standard Gateway setup. Missing runtime, browser binary, attach configuration or headed display is reported through existing Browser availability/errors; there is no controller-local fallback. Human login or challenge completion happens directly in an available headed browser; ask_user requests continuation, never passwords in chat.

Web and Browser page content remain untrusted evidence. Page instructions cannot grant capabilities, reveal secrets or authorize unrelated actions. Web Research is not a stealth scraper, CAPTCHA solver, cookie extractor or provider-specific API framework. Legal, geographic and site access controls remain restrictions. No helper model, browser planner or DOM-summary model is added. The existing selector/Task Contract call budget is unchanged.

Compatibility and limits

The Skill IDs, primitive Web/Browser argument contracts, provider configuration, permission schema and capability defaults remain unchanged. Browser snapshot/find responses include their existing public page URL and tab ID so evidence can bind to the observed page. Old conversations without research state load normally; state is initialized lazily when Web Research participates. There is no database migration or automatic certification of old free-form answers.

Typed extraction supports known JSON fields, existing Browser tables, labeled text and exact quotations. It is not a general semantic entailment engine or a provider scraper. Unsupported semantic constraints remain unresolved in the contract; the gate's matching summary concerns its represented filters. Complex substitutions, provider pagination completeness and natural-language fact normalization require additional adapters or stronger accepted intent records. An unavailable authenticated source or missing seller country remains unverified.

Run scripts/benchmarks/web_research_reliability.py --runs 5 with the configured model for the release benchmark. It uses isolated state, controlled HTTP fixtures and a disposable Chromium profile, and records fixture accuracy, useful outcomes, token/call counts and latency. See the engineering hardening report for the measured release verdict; unit tests alone are not a model reliability claim.
